text:
sara: seeing intermittent gRPC stalls between model-serving pods on node-pair eu-west-1a -> eu-west-1b. high retransmits in grafana, tails show streams pausing for ~4-6s then resume :confused:

matt: timeline? started after the rolling patch yesterday?

sara: started ~03:20 UTC, right after we rolled kernel bump to 6.4 on the dedicated-gpu pool. only affects east-west traffic, north-south to control plane looks fine.

devon: can you paste tcpdump snippet and the pod logs? also are we on calico IPIP or VXLAN for that cluster?

sara: calico VXLAN. tcpdump on node shows lots of ICMP frag-needed and then bursts of retransmit on the gRPC stream. sample: `IP 10.10.32.45.56784 > 10.10.48.12.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:13000, ack 54321, win 65535, length 655` then `ICMP frag-needed mtu 1400` repeatedly.

jules: sounds like PMTU discovery is tripping. overlay+encap lowered effective MTU to 1450, but kernel offloads (GSO/GRO) are producing larger frames that get clipped at the node egress. When that happens gRPC streaming stalls due to retransmit/backpressure.

nora: we saw similar with RDMA-enabled nodes where SR-IOV + encap made path MTU inconsistent. Are the affected nodes using SR-IOV or ena drivers?

sara: GPU nodes use ena + mlx5 (SR-IOV VF) in some AZs. the kernel bump tightened handling of oversized GSO packets.

matt: quick mitigation: clamp PMTU on the sending nodes to overlay MTU and disable GSO/GRO for the NICs as a hotfix. that should stop large offloaded frames being sent.

devon: steps?

matt: on the host: `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1450` (but that breaks host-host expectations). safer: add sysctl to clamp via rp_filter? actually we used `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` before. for UDP/gRPC over HTTP2 (TLS) TCPMSS helps for the TCP handshake path. also: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` on affected nodes.

jules: note: disabling offloads raises CPU on networking path — do on canary nodes first. alternatively, set calico's `veth mtu` to 1400 so containers never try to send large segments.

sara: trying iptables clamp on one node now, will mirror traffic to tcpdump.

infra-bot: deploy started by sara on node gpu-azb-12: iptables rule applied (id=clamp-1749999999).

sara: initial results: CPU up ~6% on envoy sidecar, but the gRPC stall rate dropped 90% for that nodepair. graph: link to internal grafana (redacted).

nora: can we make a cluster-wide fix? we have ~12% of pool with SR-IOV-enabled NICs where ethtool toggles have different semantics.

jules: plan: 1) run `ethtool -k` audit across pool to classify nodes; 2) push iptables clamp at kube-proxy DaemonSet level (mangle POSTROUTING); 3) adjust calico/vxlan MTU to 1400 and cordon+drain a few nodes to rotate. also add a BPF check for ICMP frag-needed rate to alert early.

devon: we should also test with iperf3 + --mtu and a real gRPC stream to confirm. create a canary job that streams ~500MB across pod pairs in each AZ and measures stall/retransmit.

matt: beware cost: draining and re-provisioning GPU nodes will spike spot replacements. coordinate with capacity team.

sara: filed a ticket with support for mlx5 driver regression (link to internal ticket).

infra-bot: incident severity set to P2 by sara.

nora: timeline for cluster-wide rollout? we can do iptables clamp DS this evening, calico MTU change in a maintenance window next week.

jules: also consider kernel rollback on a small subset if driver root cause is proven. but clamp+offloads toggle is lower risk.

matt: note for postmortem: include sequence numbers of gRPC stream stalls, packet captures, and the kernel config change. and add a test to CI that verifies path MTU under overlay encap stays >= container MTU.

sara: updating incident doc and will post runbook steps in #incidents. thanks all. :thumbsup:
